title: US defaults on debt by 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government fails to make a scheduled payment on any Treasury note, bond, or bill at any point between November 5, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, or Fitch publicly classify any U.S. sovereign debt as being in default during the qualifying period this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch.

eventMetadata.context_description: The recent $5 trillion debt ceiling increase enacted in the 2025 reconciliation legislation has extended the Treasury's borrowing authority to $41.1 trillion, with forecasters projecting the limit will next be approached in mid-to-late 2027. Congress has raised or suspended the statutory limit more than 100 times historically without a payment default, relying on extraordinary measures and last-minute agreements when needed. Trader consensus at 97% against default by the end of 2027 reflects this pattern of resolution, combined with strong institutional incentives to preserve Treasury market confidence and avoid broader economic disruption. Even so, prolonged legislative gridlock during the 2027 ceiling debate or an unforeseen fiscal shock could still narrow the margin for timely action.
